newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee stock error had minimal impact-analyst.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee stock error had minimal impact-analyst.

text.p: A reporting error announced late on Wednesday in certified coffee stocks at the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange was unlikely to have had a substantial effect on futures prices, said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.

A sharp, 24,391-bag drawdown for the week ended October 18 and reported on Monday was actually due to "past errors in reporting" by one warehouse, the CSCE said in a statement, but the total 5,583 bag inventory level reported was correct.

"It's possible that the market would have gone up reflecting the tight situation that much sooner," Ganes said. "But you can't say that this was a huge error on the part of the CSCE or that it caused extreme volatility in the (market), because the market was going to go (up) anyway."
"Stocks are so low that they're practically non-existent anyway," she added. "Everyone knew that they were low and they would evenually go to zero."

The exchange did not say in the statement when the coffee might have left exchange warehouses, nor did it name the warehouse responsible for the errors. No one at the exchange was available for comment.
The CSCE certified cache has fallen dramatically this year, to its lowest level in at least a decade, as roasters depleted existing inventories ahead of the arrival of the 1996/97 harvest.

New York's spot December futures contract has surged 6.30 cents per lb to a new two-month high since Monday's report of the stock drop, which would have represented a decline of more than 80 percent in exchange certified inventories.
Ganes dismissed the possibility that the reporting error might have resulted from an effort on the part of a market operator to manipulate prices.
"Errors occur in warehouse counting," she said. "I think it is a legitimate thing for a warehouse to have some sort of error that they realize all of the sudden."
"Anyone that was short the December contract would have run into difficulties anyway because there just isn't the supply around."
